# Trim guide (XE, SE and S/C)

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Remove the existing steering wheel to install a new leather-wrapped replacement. [t1850]

Pull side plastic panels outward with ratchet straps and work headliner fabric out from under the shell. [t1457]

[Partial] Remove the headliner completely from the ceiling. [t1457]

[Partial] Remove the stock incandescent bulb from the climate control panel and select a T-Series instrument cluster LED bulb. [t2233]

[Partial] Remove the original seat and inspect the replacement SE seat pan. [t1226]

Lay vinyl flooring over the existing floor area then cut custom access holes. [t1227]

Apply a homemade long varnish to the headlight lens instead of using a standard UV coat. [t1482]

Polish the headlight lens using Mother's Mag & Aluminum Polish then buff it off. [t1482]

[Partial] Apply a Meguiar's Heavy Duty Headlight Restoration Kit to the lens. [t1482]

Apply an Armor All Restoration Kit to the headlight lens and buff it off. [t1482]

[Partial] Apply Turtle Wax Restoration to the headlight lens. [t1482]

Leave the stock water temperature sensor in place and use its single wire for an aftermarket gauge. [t1852]

[Partial] Remove the broken fender plastic doohickey from all four corners. [t1313]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Pull the side plastic panels outward slightly using ratchet straps.
2. [Partial] Carefully work the headliner fabric out from under the shell, being mindful not to bend the delicate material.

_Procedure reported by [t1457]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1457] [Partial]</summary>

1. Remove the headliner completely from the ceiling.
2. Scrub dried foam residue off the roof using an upholstery attachment on a shop vac or with a wire brush.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t2233] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Remove the stock incandescent bulb from the climate control panel.
2. [Partial] Select a T-Series instrument cluster LED bulb with 360-degree light dispersion.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1226] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Remove the original seat from the vehicle.
2. [Partial] Inspect the replacement SE seat pan to ensure it matches the XE unit.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1227] [Partial]</summary>

1. Lay the vinyl flooring over the existing floor area.
2. [Partial] Cut custom access holes for every component underneath.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1482] [Partial]</summary>

1. Apply a homemade long varnish to the headlight lens instead of using a standard UV coat.
2. Mix spar urethane with boiled linseed oil and thin it down with mineral spirits.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1482] [Partial]</summary>

1. Polish the headlight lens using Mother's Mag & Aluminum Polish.
2. Buff off the polish with an orbital buffer.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1482] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Apply a Meguiar's Heavy Duty Headlight Restoration Kit to the lens.
2. Skip using the UV coat supplied in the kit if you prefer.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1482] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Apply Armor All Restoration Kit to the headlight lens.
2. [Partial] Buff off with a cloth or similar method.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1852] [Partial]</summary>

1. Leave the stock water temperature sensor in place near the front of the engine block.
2. Use the single-wire connection on that front sensor to feed a new aftermarket gauge.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1313] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Remove the broken fender plastic doohickey from all four corners.
2. Decide whether to replace them with new parts or simply leave them off.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1482] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Apply Turtle Wax Restoration to the headlight lens.

</details>

## Tips & gotchas

- Be careful about bending the plastic shell as it is very delicate. [t1457]
- [Partial] Check for four push-pin style clips that pop into the ceiling before starting, as missing them can prevent removal. [t1457]
- Use strong, heat-resistant spray adhesive for reattachment. [t1457]
- Consider painting the headliner if fabric thickness makes fitting sun visors difficult. [t1457]
- [Partial] Punch holes in the fabric of the lower pad skirt if adjustment rods do not align. [t1226]
- [Partial] Use this finish if you have woodworking experience or raw materials on hand. [t1482]
- This method is better for sunny, hot regions than standard commercial kits. [t1482]
- [Partial] This method is more economical than buying a full restoration kit and requires less frequent re-application. [t1482]
- [Partial] It may last 6-8 years with application every few months. [t1482]
- [Partial] This specific kit can keep headlights clear for one year. [t1482]
- Note that this specific kit may start hazing over 5-6 months after application. [t1482]
- This option works well for matching a new factory-installed headlight to an older one. [t1482]
- Consider removing these pieces when lifting the vehicle and installing bigger tires in the future, as this may become common practice. [t1313]
- [Partial] Note that all four corners are typically broken simultaneously. [t1313]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Forgetting to remove seat belts if necessary (though often not needed). [t1457]
- Failing to account for fabric thickness when reinstalling sun visor screws. [t1457]
- Using glue that isn't heat resistant causing it to fall down after a few days. [t1457]
